steps.label: Finding Things on the Internet
steps.content:
6.3 Computer Networks

Finding Things on the Internet

Year 6

  • Today: how data finds the right computer.
  • Where the pages you look at on the internet come from.
  • Follow data to the right computer in the 3D lab.
Think → Pair → ShareThere are millions of computers on the internet. Predict: how does a message find the one computer it is for?Show the answer

Each computer has something that is only its own, and the message carries it, so the routers know where to send it.

steps.label: Every Device Has an Address
steps.content:
Every Device Has an Address

Think → Pair → ShareA class has 30 laptops on one network. Ana sends a message to Ben. Predict: how does the network know which laptop is Ben's?Show the answer

Each laptop has its own number. The message carries Ben's number, so it goes to Ben and no one else.

  • Every device on a network has its own address: a number, like 192.168.1.3.
  • Data carries the address of the device it is going to.
  • Switches and routers read the address and send the data the right way.
  • On the internet it is called an IP address. Every device on the internet has one.

steps.label: Predict: Who Gets It?
steps.content:
Predict: Who Gets It?

Think → Pair → ShareA pizza is going to a house on a long street. Why does the driver need the house number, not only the street name?Show the answer

Many houses are on one street. The number picks out exactly one house.

Look at the address under each device.

items.prompt: Ana sends a message to 10.0.0.2. Which device gets it?
items.explain: Chi's address is 10.0.0.2, so the message goes to Chi.

items.prompt: Ben prints. Which address does his data carry?
items.explain: The data carries the address of the device it is going to: the Printer, 10.0.0.7.

steps.label: Compare: Two the Same?
steps.content:
Compare: Two the Same?

Think → Pair → ShareLook at the right picture. Ben and Chi both have the address 192.168.1.3. Predict: a message goes to 192.168.1.3. What happens, and why?Show the answer

The network cannot tell which laptop the message is for. It may not arrive, or it may go to the wrong laptop.

  • If two devices have the same address, data cannot tell which one it is for.
  • So every device on a network must have a different address, like the houses on a street.

steps.label: Activity 1: Every Device Has an Address
steps.content:
Activity 1: Every Device Has an Address

Think → Pair → ShareWhy send a message before you give Chi a new address?Show the answer

You see it fail first. Then you know the address was the problem.

Do the missions on the right in order: Every Device Has an Address, then Two the Same? Predict before you send. Walk with W A S D.

steps.label: Where Is a Website Kept?
steps.content:
Where Is a Website Kept?

Think → Pair → ShareYou open a website about cats. It is not saved on your laptop. Predict: where do its pages come from?Show the answer

From another computer, far away on the internet. It keeps the pages and sends them to anyone who asks.

  • A website, like www.cats.example, is kept on a web server.
  • A web server is a computer on the internet. It has its own address.
  • Your laptop asks the web server for a page. The web server sends the page back, in packets, router to router.

steps.label: The Internet and the Web
steps.content:
The Internet and the Web

Think → Pair → SharePeople say "the internet" and "the web" as if they mean the same thing. Predict: are they the same? Why, or why not?Show the answer

No. The internet is the networks and routers that carry data. The web is the web pages on web servers. The internet carries the web pages to you.

  • The World Wide Web (the web) is all the web pages kept on web servers.
  • The internet is the networks joined by routers. It carries the web pages to you.
  • The internet carries other things too, like messages and video calls.

steps.label: Predict: Internet or Web?
steps.content:
Predict: Internet or Web?

Think → Pair → ShareRoads and shops: why are the roads not the same thing as the shops?Show the answer

The roads carry you to the shops. The shops hold the things you want.

items.prompt: Which is the World Wide Web?
options: All the networks joined by routers
All the web pages kept on web servers
items.explain: The web is the web pages. The networks and routers are the internet.

items.prompt: What carries a web page from the web server to your laptop?
options: The internet: routers pass it on
items.explain: The page travels in packets across the internet, router to router.

items.prompt: You open www.games.example. Where do its pages come from?
items.explain: Websites are kept on web servers. Your laptop asks, and the server sends the pages.

steps.label: Trace a Website
steps.content:
Trace a Website

Think → Pair → ShareA website is slow to open. Predict: how could you find out which way its data goes, and where it comes from?Show the answer

List every router on the way, one at a time, until you reach the computer that keeps the website.

  • A trace lists each hop on the way to a website: every router, then its web server.
  • Each hop shows its address.
  • The last hop is the web server that keeps the website.
  • Different websites can be kept on different web servers, with different addresses.
Trace route to www.cats.example
1.Home router192.168.1.1
2.Router A81.2.3.1
3.Router B81.2.3.2
4.Web server203.0.113.7

steps.label: Predict: Read the Trace
steps.content:
Predict: Read the Trace

Think → Pair → ShareWhy might two websites have traces that end at different addresses?Show the answer

Each website can be kept on its own web server, and each web server has its own address.

Read the trace.

Trace route to www.games.example
1.Home router192.168.1.1
2.Router A81.2.3.1
3.Router C81.2.3.3
4.Web server198.51.100.4

items.prompt: What is the address of the web server that keeps www.games.example?
items.explain: The last hop is the web server: 198.51.100.4. The others are routers.

items.prompt: How many routers are on the way to the web server?
items.explain: Home router, Router A, Router C: 3 routers. Hop 4 is the web server, not a router.
